w: A canalised stretch of the River Lea running from Hertford Castle Weir down to the Thames at Bow Creek, threading past Enfield on its way south. Hertford Lock marks its top end and Bow Locks its bottom - a working towpath route that once carried freight and now carries walkers and cyclists the length of the Lea Valley.
s: Canalised River Lea running past Enfield to the Thames
_facts: Runs from Hertford Castle Weir to the Thames at Bow Creek
First lock is Hertford Lock, last is Bow Locks
A canalised section of the River Lea, also called the Lee

w: A Catholic parish at the junction of Stonard Road and Green Lanes, one of only two churches in the Diocese of Westminster dedicated to Saint Monica (the other is St Monica's Priory in Hoxton). It grew from a mission church into a full parish, its presbytery added in 1931, and still runs community programmes today.
s: One of only two St Monica's churches in the diocese
_facts: One of only two Diocese of Westminster parishes dedicated to St Monica
Grew from a mission church into a full parish

w: The original parish church of Enfield, standing at the heart of what is now Enfield Town. This Church of England building holds Grade II* listed status, marking it as a site of particular historic and architectural importance in the borough's old town centre.
s: Enfield's original parish church, Grade II* listed
_facts: The original parish church of Enfield
